function_v0.doc:
Whitelist a forwarding target. the target only becomes
eligible for `forward_funds` once the target activation timelock has
elapsed (see `TargetConfig::eligible_at`), so a compromised manager
cannot register a custody address and drain to it in the same block.
Removal/deactivation stay instant \xe2\x80\x94 the fail-safe direction.
function_v0.name: add_target

function_v0.doc:
the seed vault is validated against the vault's live config
(see the registry seeding below), so `config.vault` must already be an
*initialized* SToken naming this proxy as its `asset_manager`. Deploy
order: deploy proxy \xe2\x86\x92 initialize vault (with the proxy address) \xe2\x86\x92
initialize proxy.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc: Current address holding the `upgrader` role (if any).
function_v0.name: get_upgrader

function_v0.doc:
Return funds from proxy custody to a registered stoken vault.
Allowed even when paused (returning liquidity is always beneficial).

the destination `vault` is caller-supplied and must be present
in the registry. This lets the (trusted) processor return liquidity to
the correct creditor among swap-sibling vaults sharing this proxy, rather
than being hardwired to a single construction-time vault. The proxy holds
no per-vault accounting, so routing the *correct amount* to the *correct
vault* remains a processor responsibility; the vault side still guards
its own balance (`InsufficientBalance`) against over-crediting.
function_v0.name: return_funds

function_v0.doc: Forward funds from proxy custody to a whitelisted target's custody.\nCallable by manager or processor with respective limit enforcement.
function_v0.name: forward_funds

function_v0.doc:
Apply the pending WASM upgrade after the upgrade timelock expires.

Applies exactly the hash recorded by `propose_upgrade`; the caller cannot
substitute a different hash here.
function_v0.name: accept_upgrade

function_v0.doc: Cancel a pending WASM upgrade before it is applied.
function_v0.name: cancel_upgrade

function_v0.doc:
Admit a vault to the registry so the proxy may return liquidity to it.

`swap_tokens` forces swap-sibling vaults to share one
`asset_manager` address. When that shared manager is this proxy, it must
be able to return funds to *either* sibling \xe2\x80\x94 not just the vault bound at
construction \xe2\x80\x94 otherwise a sibling's deployed capital is permanently
stranded. Registration is validated so the entry is actually usable:

* the vault must use this proxy's `underlying_asset` (the proxy custodies
a single token; routing any other token would silently misfire), and
* the vault must already name this proxy as its `asset_manager`
(otherwise `SToken::return_funds` rejects the proxy as `Unauthorized`,
making the registry entry inert).

Unlike `add_target` (timelocked since), registration takes
effect immediately: admitting a wrong vault cannot extract funds \xe2\x80\x94
`return_funds`/`emergency_sweep` only ever *credit* a vault, and the
vault-side authorization check fails closed.
function_v0.name: register_vault

function_v0.doc: Accept a pending `upgrader` change after the cooldown (admin-gated).
function_v0.name: accept_upgrader

function_v0.doc:
Re-enable a deactivated target. reactivation restarts the
eligibility timelock \xe2\x80\x94 every transition into a forwardable state must
carry the same monitoring window as a fresh registration, otherwise a
dormant entry would be an instant drain destination.
function_v0.name: activate_target

function_v0.doc:
Emergency sweep tokens from a paused proxy to a registered vault,
crediting the vault's `total_idle` via `stoken.return_funds`.
Requires proxy to be paused and emergency cooldown period elapsed.
If amount is 0, sweeps the entire balance.

the destination `vault` is caller-supplied and must be
registered. Because the proxy commingles the liquidity of every vault it
serves, this is a break-glass path: a full sweep (`amount == 0`) sends
the *entire* pooled balance to the single supplied vault, so when the
proxy serves multiple vaults the manager must sweep per-vault amounts and
reconcile the remainder off-chain rather than dumping everything to one
creditor.
function_v0.name: emergency_sweep

function_v0.doc:
Propose a WASM upgrade. Starts the fixed upgrade timelock
([`UPGRADE_COOLDOWN_SECS`]) before the new code can be applied.

WASM replacement is the most powerful operation in the proxy, so it is
split into a timelocked propose/accept flow. The proposed hash is
recorded and bound: `accept_upgrade` applies exactly this hash, so the
timelock cannot be bypassed by proposing a benign hash and later
applying a different one.
function_v0.name: propose_upgrade

function_v0.doc: Remove a vault from the registry (manager-gated). After removal the proxy\ncan no longer route `return_funds`/`emergency_sweep` to that vault.
function_v0.name: deregister_vault

function_v0.doc: Propose a new `upgrader` (admin-gated). Starts the cooldown timelock.\nThe upgrader controls WASM replacement, so rotation is restricted to the\nadmin (the role-admin of `upgrader`), never the operational manager.
function_v0.name: propose_upgrader
